text:
maria: Quick dump from last night's perf run — new KV warmup cut cold-miss rate but we have a regression on 8k-context mixed loads. p95 up ~12% on a few models.

ajay: Can you paste the flamegraphs/traces or a top-line profile?

maria: Top of perf summary pasted below:
```text
model: redwood-bert-8k
workload: mixed init+gen (30% prefill-heavy, 70% decode-stream)
p95_latency: baseline 48ms -> now 54ms
kv_hit_rate: baseline 0.87 -> now 0.71 after change
kernel_fallbacks: +220 ops/min (generic matmul)
```

kevin: Kernel selector is falling back to the generic matmul on some attention ops — sequence-length branch seems to misclassify when batch contains mixed-phase tokens.

lex: Hypothesis: continuous batcher is forming batches that mix long prefill sequences and short decode streams. The selector sees a noisy seq-len distribution and picks a conservative kernel.

maria: Exactly. Runtime currently builds continuous batches without phase metadata; prefill tokens get merged with decode tokens in the formation window and skew the kernel decision. Also noticed KV gets thrashed when prefill-heavy requests get GPU priority.

ajay: Proposal: add a simple phase tag at queue insertion and prefer grouping by dominant phase in the batch-formation window. Also add token-budget targets: prefill_budget=4096, decode_budget=512 as defaults for the canary.

kevin: We tried a soft split last sprint — helped average latency but tail spiked due to backlog on the smaller queue. Need smarter queue backoff (thresholds + slow-start).

maria: Attached sampling trace id `SAMPLE_ID: abc123` — you can see kv_hit_rate drops immediately after kernel switch and evictions spike. Looks like prefill steals cache lines and warmup parity breaks.

lex: Could add prefer-kv-warmup policy: if batch is flagged prefill-dominant, force the kernel that preserves KV layout (even if slightly slower FLOPS). Might reduce evictions.

ajay: Alternative: if decode queue occupancy > 0.6, delay enqueuing prefill into the same formation window by N ms. Keeps decode latency predictable.

kevin: Also revisit kernel-score heuristic: current weights (0.7 FLOPS, 0.3 memory) bias toward heavy compute paths; for long-seq prefill batches we should increase memory weight. Suggest flipping to (0.4 FLOPS, 0.6 memory) for seq_len>1024.

maria: I'll run an A/B: phase-aware grouping + token budgets + kernel-score flip on a small canary. Need a dedicated canary pool.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled on pool-3 at 07:30 UTC — job runtime-canary/kv-phase-a-b created.

lex: If canary is green, add two dashboard widgets: KV eviction rate and kernel_fallback_rate (per model). Also surface the batch-phase-mix ratio.

maria: Will add a micro-benchmark that explicitly mixes prefill+decode slices to reproduce locally and attach results here.

ajay: Experiment checklist: p95 latency, kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, tokens/sec, and queue_fill_ratio. Run > 30m to get stable tails.

kevin: Keep a rollback plan: if p95 tails get worse, revert phase-splitting and try windowed batching with prefer-sample ordering.

maria: Thanks — starting runs now, will drop the canary logs and a short summary when done. :thumbsup:
